Part Two

What is an LLM?

2
A new kind of resource:
general-purpose intelligence,
bought by the token
(kind of)
From outside, looking in
f : String -> String

Outside the API boundary, this is the observable behaviour.

No hidden state is carried between calls.

Nondeterministic

"What is spin?"

→

"Spin is..."

"Angular..."

"In QM..."

Same input, different outputs: the model samples from P(next token | context)

Temperature
P(token_i) = exp(ℓ_i/T) / Σ_j exp(ℓ_j/T)
0.1 · ground state3.0 · hot
The electron has

Direct analogy to the Boltzmann distribution. Low T freezes into the ground state; high T melts toward uniform.

Tokens

Not characters. Not words.

Subword chunks from a fixed vocabulary V of about 100k entries.

'theoretical physics' -> ['theor', 'etical', ' physics']

More precisely: f : Token* → Token*

An LLM is a stateless, nondeterministic function
f : String -> String
that samples from P(next_token | context)
via a single forward pass through a frozen neural network
The context window

Everything the model sees is one token sequence, capped at a fixed length: the context window

re-sent in full with every message
system prompt
user
assistant
user
assistant▌
free
hidden from the user
being generated right now
room to grow

Current models: 200k to 1M tokens (a million tokens is roughly two thousand pages)

Part Three

The illusion of chat

3
How chat works
Turn 1: [user_1] Turn 2: [user_1, asst_1, user_2] Turn 3: [user_1, asst_1, user_2, asst_2, user_3]

The client re-sends the entire history every turn: the LLM has no memory.

The agent loop
while not done: response = llm(system_prompt + history) tool_calls = parse(response) results = execute(tool_calls) history += [response, results]

It generates text; your scaffolding acts on it.

Fresh adversarial check

Reliable computation out of unreliable components

The filesystem is permanent memory
disksurvives every wipe

Every session forgets. The files do not.

Errors compound

A flat chain of thought has no error detection. If each step succeeds with probability 1 − ε:

P(the whole derivation) = (1 − ε)ⁿ
per-step error
1%
steps
100
survive intact
37%

A slip at step 3 propagates silently to step 40, while the trace stays locally fluent throughout.

This is why long unchecked derivations rot

Supervisor

delegates and composes reports

fresh context

Each worker gets a clean window; results return as short reports.

Context isolation is the point

Three ways to spend compute on reliability
(a) flat chain. One slip at step 3; everything after it is quietly wrong.
(b) parallel repetition. Majority vote over final answers. Helps, but scales poorly with depth.
(c) recursive decomposition. Verify each block in isolation; expand the one that fails.

(c) is the concatenated-code strategy (von Neumann, 1956).

Above the verification threshold, reliability compounds instead of decaying

What the Swiss cheese produces

364 results · 769 dependency edges · every arrow is a checked contract

the whole argument
A registry of one-line contracts. A linker refuses any edge from a rigorous result to an unrigorous one, so the colour of a node is an upper bound on everything above it.
Near the top of the validated chain: an interface lemma. Everything it rests on is green, and each green node was proved by one fresh agent and attacked by another.
The open problem itself. What it still rests on is orange and red: the gap is visible, named, and exactly where the next agent gets sent.
One agent proves, a fresh one attacks, a linker keeps the ledger. The colour is what survived.
Agents are amazing at helping you understand

Three agents, in parallel, each turned the paper, the referee report, an explainer and a one-page brief into a five-slide interactive explainer.
Time
All three were back within 40 minutes. I picked one.

Purity as a spotlight
Gibbs purity T(n,β) = Σk pk2 = Zn(2β)/Zn(β)2
spatial purity S(n,β) = Σi qi2 = Z2n(β)/Zn(β)2 (keys [ ] for β, − = for n)
Purity ≥ 1 − u with u < ½ forces one state of weight ≥ 1 − u: a unique ground state, and e−βγ ≤ u/(1−u).

The flow
uj+1 = C uj2, βj = 2jβ0, nj = 2jn0, gap bound log(1/3uj)/βj
seed as in the paper: (60, 105/4), u0 = 1/8, C = 7.9 (keys [ ] for u0, − = for C)
Gapless chain: finite-size gap ≈ v/n, correlation length ≈ vβ. T → 1 needs vβ ≫ n, S → 1 needs n ≫ vβ. Best compromise: defects 0.3 to 0.5, above the 1/8 the machine needs. Gapped: ξ and 1/Δ finite, the two demands decouple.
A finite ring that looks gapped on both axes with margin 1/8 looks gapped at every larger scale. Even sizes in between: Hölder on the spatial weights.
ladder computed live from the paper's seed values (Prop 4.3, 5.4: u₀ ≤ 1/8, C < 7.9); critical defects 0.3 to 0.5: the review's estimate · openai/math, family 268, read 7 Oct 2026
The fine print
what is proved, what was checked, where a bug would hide
Theorem 1.1
HL = Σj Sj·Sj+1, spin 1, periodic. Every even L ≥ 60: unique ground state and γL > (4/105) log(80/79) ≈ 4.8·10−4. Every even L ≥ 2304: γL > log 20 / 784 ≈ 3.8·10−3. Hence liminf γL > 0.
Scope
Even periodic rings and the liminf of their gaps. Cor 6.1 gives a gap inequality for subsequential limits of periodic ground states, not uniqueness or a gap for every infinite-volume ground state. True gap ≈ 0.41: the constants are a thousand times smaller.
The seeds
Where the labour is. (60, 105/4) from exact Zn, n ≤ 10, at β = 21/2 (59,049 states, exact integers, rigorous series truncation), polynomial filters on the spectrum, a bond-dimension-26 MPS giving Z120 > 1, a 5/2-power raise of β. Margin: S(60,105/4) > 7/8 by 6·10−4. Second seed (36, 49/4): defects 0.048 and 0.18, six doublings to (2304, 784).
Verification
No Lean. Exact-rational scalar scripts and both MPS contractions re-run and pass; tightest margins 4.7·10−5 and 6·10−4. Independent exact diagonalisation reproduces the tables for n ≤ 9. Unverified: Z10(21/2), which the L ≥ 60 theorem needs, and n = 10 to 12 at β = 49/4.
Verdict
One reviewer, one pass: no mathematical error found. 85 to 90% that the theorem is proved as written, conditional on the n = 10 to 12 integer totals. If a bug hides anywhere, it is in the seeds, not in the doubling.
